Examples.Title: S-Parameters
Examples.Summary: A Touchstone black box swept for gain and stability, and a pair of coupled inductors. Stability factors K and mu are written as measurement expressions.

Examples.Title: Harmonic Balance
Examples.Summary: A 48 V GaN power amplifier driven into compression, and the same amplifier under two tones for IM2/IM3/IM5. The FET is a reusable sub-cell.

Examples.Title: Loadpull and Pursuit
Examples.Summary: The same device swept over a polar load grid (LP), and again with the pursuit search walking to the optimum (LPP).

Examples.Title: Klopfenstein Taper vs MoM
Examples.Summary: A 50-to-100 ohm taper solved twice: once from the closed-form model, once by the planar EM engine. Run the EM setup and compare.

Examples.Title: Patch Antenna
Examples.Summary: A 5.8 GHz microstrip patch with an inset feed, set up for a full-wave planar solve with a radiation pattern.

Examples.Title: PDK PCells (Python artwork)
Examples.Summary: A parameterised microstrip line, two spiral inductors and a MIM capacitor whose layout artwork is generated by Python. The kit ships inside the workspace.

Examples.Title: System Design (TX and RX)
Examples.Summary: A 2.4 GHz transmitter and receiver drawn twice — direct conversion and superheterodyne — from the System block library, plus a transmitter whose final stage is a nonlinear FET and a cascade gain/IP3/noise budget.

Examples.Title: Power Rail Integrity
Examples.Summary: A four-layer board with one 3.3 V rail: the DC drop and where it goes, Z(f) against a flat target, and which of thirteen capacitors are actually doing anything.

Examples.Title: Smith Chart (narrowband match)
Examples.Summary: A device input of 8 − j12 Ω, stated over three frequencies, matched to 50 Ω by hand with a series L and a shunt C. Drag either gripper and watch the band edges move.
